penalties_applied.name: b2c_at_scale_needed
penalties_applied.reason: Students and self-directed learners are individual consumers at low price points ($3–8/mo realistic); reaching break-even requires hundreds to thousands of paying users, which is beyond what a solo operator can drive without a significant acquisition budget or viral loop.

rationale: Students who watch YouTube for learning encounter this problem frequently, but they are notoriously price-sensitive and rarely pay for note-taking tools when free alternatives (ChatGPT, Notion AI free tier, browser extensions) exist. The buyer is an individual consumer (not a business), willingness to pay is weak, and the space is already crowded with free-to-cheap competitors. The total falls well below the 5.5 validate threshold.
solution_plan: This opportunity is not recommended for pursuit. While the factory could build a Claude-powered YouTube-to-Cornell-notes tool in a week (transcript extraction + Claude formatting prompt + a simple web page + Stripe), the student consumer market is too price-sensitive and crowded to generate meaningful revenue without large-scale paid acquisition. A solo operator cannot win this market economically.
notes: Total 3.7 is below min_total_to_validate (5.5). buyer_clarity (3) and willingness_to_pay (4) are the key weaknesses. Drop.
